user_rationale: Brief explanation of why user chose this strategy (2-3 sentences)

domain_based.when_to_use: Clear domain boundaries, low coordination requirements, CRUD-heavy operations
pros: Easy to understand for domain experts
cons: Coordination logic becomes distributed state management

workflow_based.when_to_use: High coordination requirements, cross-domain workflows, workflow-heavy operations
pros: Common workflows self-contained in one service
Fewer service-to-service calls for common operations
Easier to reason about workflow state
cons: May duplicate some domain logic across services

hybrid.description: Mix of workflow services and domain services
hybrid.when_to_use: Large, complex systems with both complex workflows and clear shared domains
pros: Flexible - choose best pattern per service
cons: Need to carefully decide which pattern per service

domain_based.service_decomposition: Group functions by business domain (User, Product, Order, Payment)
domain_based.coordination_pattern: Distributed - services coordinate via events, sagas, or orchestration
domain_based.state_management: Each service owns its domain state

workflow_based.service_decomposition: Group functions by user workflow (Checkout, Inventory, Fulfillment)
workflow_based.coordination_pattern: Local - coordination state managed within workflow service
workflow_based.state_management: Workflow services own workflow state, may access shared domain state

hybrid.service_decomposition: Identify workflow services (complex coordination) and domain services (shared capabilities)
hybrid.coordination_pattern: Hybrid - local within workflow services, distributed between domain services
hybrid.state_management: Workflow services own workflow state, domain services own domain state
hybrid.integration_pattern: Mixed - orchestration for workflows, events for domain services
